title: Proper morphisms with a relatively ample invertible module over a qcqs base are projective
statement: Let $h:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], where $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] that is $h$-relatively ample. Then $h$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Here an invertible module $L$ on the source of a morphism $h$ is $h$-relatively ample if $h$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and, for every affine open $V$ of its target, $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0BCL (lemma-projective-is-quasi-projective-proper), implication (1) from quasi-projective and proper to projective, with Definition Tag 01VW(1) (definition-quasi-projective) and Definition Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample).

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], properness of $h$ includes that $h$ is of finite type. In particular $h$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus the given relative ampleness has exactly the finite-type hypothesis required below; quasi-compactness of $S$ is part of the assumptions.

Apply [lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample] to $h$ and $L$: $h$ is of finite type by step 1 and $S$ is quasi-compact. It gives an integer $n\ge1$ such that $N=L^{\otimes n}$ is relatively very ample over $S$. In particular $N$ is invertible by [def-trf-relatively-very-ample]. This stage does not assert that the quasi-coherent module occurring in the definition of very ampleness is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 01VU (lemma-finite-type-ample-very-ample); the first reduction in the proof of Tag 07RM (lemma-quasi-projective-open-projective).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-very-ample-finite-type-realization] to $h$ and the relatively very ample invertible module $N$. Its base hypotheses are precisely the assumed quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $S$, and its finite-type hypothesis is step 1. Obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $E$ and an immersion $r:X\to\mathbf P_S(E)$ with $\pi_E\circ r=h$. This supplies finiteness of $E$ without any Noetherian or coherent-pushforward assumption.

source.place: Tag 07RM (lemma-quasi-projective-open-projective), finite-type approximation and immersion construction in the proof.

proof.text: The structure morphism $\pi_E:\mathbf P_S(E)\to S$ is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated], applicable to the quasi-coherent module $E$ of step 3. In the commutative triangle $X\xrightarrow{r}\mathbf P_S(E)\xrightarrow{\pi_E}S$, the composite is the given proper morphism $h$. Therefore [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] gives that $r$ is proper.

The morphism $r$ is an immersion by step 3 and proper by step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes $r$ a closed immersion. Now $h=\pi_E\circ r$ presents $X$ over $S$ as a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P_S(E)$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent module $E$. This is exactly projectivity in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BCL (lemma-projective-is-quasi-projective-proper), proof of the converse in (1), and Tag 01W8 (definition-projective); Schemes Tag 01IQ (lemma-immersion-when-closed).
